Story & Plot

Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam follows public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam as he takes on one of the most high-profile criminal cases in India's history during the trial of Ajmal Kasab following the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. The biographical drama revisits defining criminal trials in Indian history, exploring legal battles and Pakistan's role in sponsoring terrorism. Nikam must confront the immense personal and professional burden of a case that defines his legacy in his unwavering pursuit of justice.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film primarily focuses on high-stakes courtroom drama and the gravity of historical criminal trials rather than heavy humor. Comedy elements are minimal, with brief comedic moments by Karunesh Talwar, though the core narrative remains grounded in a serious crime and drama genre.

Performances & Direction

Rajkummar Rao delivers a standout performance as public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam, capturing the immense burden of the high-profile case. Wamiqa Gabbi, Jaideep Ahlawat, Sikandar Kher, Ashish Vidhyarthi, and Ritvik Sahore round out the cast with strong support, contributing significantly to the dramatic weight of the feature.

Strengths

  • Honest portrayal of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks
  • Standout performances by Rajkummar Rao and Jaideep Ahlawat
  • Skillful navigation of a sensitive narrative
  • Avoidance of heavy-handed propaganda

Weaknesses

Reviewers note that the first half of the film feels stretched and that unnecessary family drama parts tend to weigh down the pacing, suggesting a tighter runtime would have benefited the narrative.

Final verdict

Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam offers an honest, commendable look at a defining chapter in Indian legal history anchored by powerful lead performances. While pacing issues in the first half and some unnecessary family drama elements hold it back, it succeeds as a rare, propaganda-avoiding courtroom drama. Recommended for viewers interested in biographical crime dramas and high-stakes legal proceedings.

The film leans more heavily into its terrifying premise and thriller elements than any lighthearted humor. The entertainment value hinges on the tension of Aman's desperate situation with his boss and the supernatural threat he encounters. Weaknesses

The Last Ride offers a dark, supernatural ride with an interesting migrant worker premise and an eerie witch encounter, but its execution stumbles.
